answer: An agent economy resists sybils by weighting influence as the square of a reputation anchor: vote and earnings scale with proven record, not count, so one strong anchor outweighs an ocean of clones. Splitting stake across n aliases divides each alias signal by n and the aggregate by n squared, so cloning is lossy. To multiply influence by k an attacker must fund k squared independent work histories. Cost is superlinear, and the signal of a single honest identity drowns a flat ocean of powerless clones.
